messages.content: Write a post about starting a mentorship program on an engineering team. Around 250 words.

output:
Clean through the repo's own `slopwatch` gate. Here it is (~245 words):

---

We started a mentorship program in March. Here's what I'd tell you before you start yours.

The version that failed first: we paired everyone with everyone, wrote a doc, and called it done. Six weeks later, four of the nine pairs had never met twice. The doc had 31 views.

What worked was smaller and more boring. We asked five senior engineers to take one person each, and then we bought them the time. Ninety minutes a week, on the calendar, defended in sprint planning like any other commitment. That last part is the whole program. Everything else is garnish.

We also killed the curriculum. The original had modules on system design, code review, and career growth, which is the kind of thing that sounds great in a planning doc and dies on contact with an actual Tuesday. Instead: bring a real problem. A PR you're stuck on. A design you can't defend. A conversation with your manager that went badly.

Two things surprised me. The seniors got more out of it than the juniors did. Three of them told me it was the first time in years anyone had asked them to explain how they think. And the pairs that worked best crossed team boundaries, where there was no reporting line and nothing to perform.

Nine months in, we've lost one pair to a reorg. The rest still meet.

If you're starting one: pick five people, protect the hour, skip the curriculum.

---

The numbers (March, 31 views, five engineers, ninety minutes, nine months) are invented placeholders — swap in your real ones, since the specifics are what keep it from reading like generic advice.
